description: Sri Lanka’s Accession to the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-11-24 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - ‘The Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership’ (RCEP) is a comprehensive Free Trade Agreement (FTA) among 10 member countries of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and five other regional countries viz. Australia, China, Japan, South Korea and New Zealand that have already entered into Free Trade Agreements with countries of the said Association. The Agreement came into effect on 2022‑01‑01 and 18 months later since then viz. July 2023, it was opened for accession for other interested countries. Under the said Agreement, the member countries shall take steps to fully liberalize tariffs ranging between 85% and 90% of their tariff lines. Accession to the said Agreement will enable Sri Lanka to diversify its exports and markets, as well as strengthen its participation in regional and global supply chains. Accordingly, Sri Lanka has submitted a Letter of Intent on 2023‑06‑28 to join the said Agreement. A preliminary questionnaire has been issued to several countries including Sri Lanka on 2025‑10‑24 in order to collect preliminary information to assess the compliance of the applicants with all the provisions and rules contained in the Agreement and their readiness and the preparation to deliver commercially meaningful market access in line with the aspirations of the Agreement and the questionnaire should be completed before 2026‑01‑25. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Trade, Commerce, Food Security and Co-operative Development for Sri Lanka's accession in the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership and for the completion and submission of the preliminary questionnaire provided to Sri Lanka, as necessary, was approved by the Cabinet.
